prerequisites: Thorough knowledge of general chemistry as taught in General and Technical Chemistry H01A8. Students are expected to be familiar with writing Lewis structures, electron structure, bond formation, electronegativity, polarity, and a basic understanding of chemical equilibrium.

learning_outcomes.text: Students can rank a given series of analogous compounds according to acidity or basicity and justify this based on electronic effects such as electronegativity, mesomerism, aromaticity, and hybridization.

Students can rank a given series of analogous compounds according to reactivity in a given reaction type such as addition, elimination, and substitution and justify this based on electronic effects such as electronegativity, mesomerism, aromaticity, and hybridization.
Students can complete a simple given synthesis sequence with reagents and/or intermediates.
Students are able to formulate a synthesis proposal themselves using observed reactions for a simple compound starting from a given raw material.
Students can explain a described experimental observation or predict the outcome of an experiment.
Students are aware that almost all products of the current chemical industry are ultimately prepared from petroleum.
Students realize that biochemical processes can be described in terms of organic chemistry.

syllabus_topics: Evaluating acidity and basicity of organic molecules
Naming geometric isomers and absolute configurations
Evaluating reactivities in electrophilic and nucleophilic additions
Practicing the application of important electrophilic and nucleophilic addition reagents
Proposing synthesis for simple molecules using electrophilic and nucleophilic addition reactions
Evaluating reactivities in electrophilic and nucleophilic substitutions
Practicing the application of important electrophilic and nucleophilic substitution reagents
Proposing synthesis for simple molecules using electrophilic and nucleophilic substitution reactions
Classifying elimination reactions according to the mechanism followed
Practicing the application of important radical reactions
Proposing synthesis for simple molecules using all learned reactions

assessment_methods.method: Written exam with open questions during the examination period

assessment_rules: The assessment consists of application questions in a written exam with open questions. No learning material is allowed during the exam.
